title: LCA extension manifest
description: Schema for the parsed form of extension.toml. The manifest is written in TOML and validated against this schema after parsing. Version 0.1, targets ABI 0.1.

name.description: Extension identity. Must match the credential namespace when the credentials capability is used. Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

version.description: Semantic version of this extension release.

abi.description: The ABI line this extension targets, as major.minor. The host loads the current minor version and the one before it.

worlds.description: The WIT worlds this component implements. The host verifies that the component exports each one.

description.description: One sentence shown in the extension list and at install time.

homepage.description: Project page. Shown at install time so a user can inspect the source.

source.description: Source repository. Shown at install time.

capabilities.description: Every capability the extension needs. A capability absent here is absent from the import table at runtime.

limits.description: Optional resource hints. The host clamps each value to its own maximum and may ignore a request that exceeds it.

memory_mb.description: Linear memory ceiling for one instance.

fuel_per_call.description: Execution budget for a single call. Exceeding it cancels the call.

hostPattern.description: An exact hostname, or a wildcard pattern with a leading '*.' matching one or more labels. A bare '*' is rejected. An optional ':port' suffix pins a non-default port; without one the grant is port 443 only. A wildcard pattern with a port is rejected at install time.

netCapability.description: Outbound HTTPS to named hosts, port 443 unless a pattern pins another port. The extension never touches a socket. The host resolves every hostname and refuses a connection whose resolved address falls in one of the local ranges the capability catalog lists, loopback, private-use, link-local, unique-local, carrier-grade NAT, even if the hostname pattern matched, to prevent DNS rebinding. See ADR-0011.

localAddressPattern.description: A literal loopback, private-use, link-local, unique-local, or carrier-grade NAT IPv4/IPv6 address, a CIDR range within those blocks, 'localhost', or an mDNS-style '.local' hostname. Whether a given CIDR actually falls within those blocks is a numeric range check the host performs at install time; this schema's pattern only constrains the lexical shape and cannot itself reject an out-of-range CIDR such as 8.8.8.0/24. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are normalized to IPv4 before range checks.

netLocalCapability.description: HTTP or HTTPS, any port, to loopback, private-use, link-local, unique-local, or carrier-grade NAT (tailnet) addresses. Separate from net because the risk shape, pattern syntax, and port/scheme rules differ. Reaches beyond the local machine to other devices on the network and the tailnet. See ADR-0011.

fsCapability.description: Access to named filesystem scopes. Scope names are validated against the host vocabulary rather than a fixed enum in the ABI, so new scopes are additive. Unknown names are rejected at install time with the list of names this host supports. Resolution never reaches the agent's own state directory (sessions, extension tree, credential store).

credentialsCapability.description: Read and write access to one namespace. The namespace must equal the extension name; there is no cross-namespace access. Whether the namespace actually matches the extension's own name is a string-equality check the host performs at install time, the same class of limitation as the net-local CIDR check above: this schema validates the namespace's shape, not that it matches this particular manifest's name field, since a plain JSON Schema cannot compare one field's value against another's.

oauthCapability.description: The loopback authorization flow. The host binds the port and parses the callback. Token exchange needs the net capability as well.

processCapability.description: The right to ask the host to run a command. Every command still passes through the user approval prompt.

reason.description: Shown verbatim at install time. A bare capability name gives the user nothing to evaluate.

ptyCapability.description: Allocation of a pseudo-terminal for an interactively spawned program, distinct from process's plain pipe-backed streams. See ADR-0016.

completionCapability.description: The right to ask the host for a response from the currently active provider. Added in 1.0 by ADR-0015. The extension never calls another extension directly; the host mediates. See ADR-0008 for why extension-to-extension calls are unsupported.

uiCapability.description: The right to render in named regions. Rendering returns a widget tree; the host draws it.

then.$comment: An oauth flow needs net to exchange the code for a token. Declaring oauth without net is a manifest error, not a runtime surprise.

A provider world reaches a model API, which is net for a hosted vendor or net-local for a local server such as LM Studio or Ollama; a provider extension with neither cannot function. Requiring net specifically would wrongly reject a local-only provider, which is why this is net-or-net-local rather than net alone.
Implementing the ui world without the ui capability means the render export is never called.

examples.name: task-tracker
examples.description: Tracks open tasks across a session and shows them in a panel.
